title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Detroit, MI: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Detroit auto, plant, refinery and utility welders: code book choice, Part B planning, experience rules. Online or on site.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Detroit: Six Days for Automotive, Plant and Utility Welding Inspectors
html:
Most welds made in southeast Michigan are never seen by a human inspector one at a time. Robots put thousands of resistance spot welds into a car body every shift, and quality is controlled by destructive teardown, process monitoring and statistics. Yet the Detroit region still employs a large number of welding inspectors, because around every assembly plant sits a ring of structural steel, tooling, conveyors, pressure piping, utility work and heavy fabrication that is inspected the traditional way: by a person with gauges, a code book and the authority to reject. For that work, employers increasingly list the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential as a requirement.

Atlantis NDT runs a six-day preparation course for the CWI exam, written for Detroit-area welders, weld technicians, quality engineers, fitters and NDT technicians who are getting ready to apply. The American Welding Society runs the exam and awards the certificate. Atlantis prepares people and does nothing beyond that; it does not certify, it does not see AWS exam content, and it has no AWS approval or endorsement. Meeting the AWS eligibility rules and the vision requirement is each candidate's own responsibility. Individual candidates take the course online, with materials, a study plan, original practice items and an instructor who answers their questions. A plant or contractor can book the six days at its own facility for a group of employees. The national course page lays out the full program day by day.

Automotive welding and where a CWI fits in it

Ford, General Motors and Stellantis run assembly, stamping, powertrain and battery operations across southeast Michigan, and hundreds of tier suppliers make frames, brackets, exhaust systems, seat structures and axles for them. The welding behind those parts is mostly resistance spot welding, gas metal arc welding by robot, and increasingly laser and aluminum joining. Automotive weld quality is usually governed by each manufacturer's own engineering standards, supplemented by the AWS D8 committee's automotive weld quality specifications, rather than by the structural codes the CWI exam is built around.

That raises a fair question: why would an auto supplier want a CWI? There are three common reasons. First, the credential proves a person understands welding processes, joint design, metallurgy and discontinuities at a level that makes them useful in a weld lab or a launch team. Second, many suppliers also build structural products, fixtures or trailers that do fall under AWS D1.1. Third, customers and auditors like to see a recognized welding qualification in the quality department.

AWS also offers a separate credential aimed squarely at this industry, the Certified Resistance Welding Technician (CRWT), which deals with spot and projection welding equipment and setup. The CWI is the broader inspection credential; the CRWT is the process specialist. Some Detroit weld engineers hold both.

Plant steel, tooling and the work around the assembly line

Outside the body shop, Detroit-area plants are full of welded steel that is inspected the conventional way. Mezzanines, crane runways, conveyor supports and paint shop structures are designed and fabricated to AWS D1.1. Dies and fixtures are repaired by welding, often on tool steels that crack easily without careful preheat and slow cooling. Plant utilities include boilers, compressed air systems and process piping built to ASME codes.

Steelmaking adds another layer. Cleveland-Cliffs operates the Dearborn Works steel mill next to Ford's Rouge complex, and mills of that kind generate steady repair and maintenance welding on heavy equipment. Atlantis supports this sector through steel NDT consulting for Detroit, and the inspection side of automotive manufacturing is described on the pages for magnetic particle testing in automotive plants and ultrasonic testing for the auto industry.

Refining, utilities and the river border

Southwest Detroit is home to Marathon Petroleum's Detroit refinery, the main refinery in Michigan. Refinery maintenance and turnarounds bring in welders and inspectors who work to ASME Section IX, ASME B31.3 and the operator's specifications, and the inspection of that equipment is a specialty of its own. Atlantis covers refinery owners through refining NDT consulting in Detroit.

Utility work is the other large source of code welding. Gas distribution and transmission lines in the region are welded to API 1104 under federal pipeline safety rules, and power plant piping follows ASME B31.1. Contractors on those projects often need a CWI on the crew.

Then there is the border. The Gordie Howe International Bridge, a large cable-stayed crossing between Detroit and Windsor overseen by the Windsor-Detroit Bridge Authority, has brought years of heavy construction, including a new US port of entry and highway interchange work by the Michigan Department of Transportation. Bridge and highway steel in Michigan is fabricated and repaired under MDOT specifications that call on AWS D1.5 for steel bridges. On building sites, Michigan applies a state code derived from the International Building Code, and its special inspection rules put third-party welding inspectors on steel-framed structures.

Detroit employers that hire welding inspectors

  • Automotive OEM and supplier quality departments hire weld engineers, weld technicians and quality inspectors. A CWI strengthens an application here, especially for roles that cover both robotic production and fabricated tooling or structures.
  • Tooling, fixture and automation builders fabricate steel frames and machine bases for assembly lines and value inspectors who know D1.1 and can check distortion and fit before machining.
  • Structural fabricators and erectors need in-house QC for buildings, plants and parking structures.
  • Testing and inspection agencies provide special inspection on building sites and third-party inspection at supplier shops. Atlantis does this work too; see third-party inspection in Detroit and weld inspection services in Detroit.
  • Mechanical and utility contractors working at the refinery, power stations and gas utilities need inspectors who handle ASME and API 1104 documents.
  • Bridge and highway consultants working for MDOT and county road agencies hire field inspectors for steel repair and new construction.

The common requirement across all of them is the ability to measure a weld, compare it with a written criterion and document the result clearly. That is the skill the exam tests, and it is where the six days concentrate.

The AWS Detroit Section and its student chapters

AWS organizes members into districts and local sections, and the Detroit Section is part of District 11, which also includes the Central Michigan, Northern Michigan and West Michigan sections. The Detroit Section has a long record of technical events tied to the auto industry. Its bulletins have advertised plant tours on both sides of the river, including a 2015 technical evening at a resistance welding equipment maker in Windsor, Ontario. In 2015 the section also announced the first AWS student chapter inside the city of Detroit, at the GoLightly vocational center.

Section meetings are a good place to meet weld engineers and inspectors who have already been through the CWI process. Ask which code book suits your employer, how they documented experience from mixed automotive roles, and how they prepared for the practical. Officers and venues change, so look up the District 11 listing on aws.org before you go.

Welding programs around the metro area

Detroit-area welders come up through community colleges, union apprenticeships, career and technical high school programs and employer training. Washtenaw Community College in Ann Arbor, which has hosted the Detroit Section's high school welding competition, offers welding and fabrication programs. Further south, Monroe County Community College has offered an associate degree in welding.

An associate degree in welding or engineering technology matters for the CWI because AWS reduces the experience requirement for candidates with that level of education. Someone who finishes a two-year program and then works in welding can reach eligibility sooner than a welder with only a high school diploma. The CWI requirements guide explains the trade-off.

How Detroit candidates sit the exam

The CWI exam is split into three parts with two delivery methods. Fundamentals, Part A, has 150 questions on a computer screen at a Prometric center. Code Application, Part C, is also computer-based at Prometric and lets you consult your chosen code book across roughly 50 to 65 questions. AWS reports over 100 Prometric locations in the United States, so southeast Michigan candidates generally have options nearby. You need the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation letter to book.

Practical, Part B, is the exception. You perform measurement and evaluation tasks with AWS-provided tools and specimens and answer 46 questions, and AWS holds it only at its seminar locations on dates linked to its seminar program. Check aws.org for the location closest to Detroit and its upcoming dates before you settle on a study plan. Each part needs a score of at least 72%.

AWS lists its exam and seminar fees on aws.org. For planning the full outlay, including books, travel to Part B and time off, use the CWI exam cost planner.

Code books: what Detroit candidates usually choose

AWS accepts one code book in Part C, from a list that includes AWS D1.1, D1.2 for aluminum, D1.5 for bridges, D15.1 for railroad equipment, D17.1 for aerospace, API 1104, an ASME choice that sets Section IX alongside the power and process piping codes (B31.1 and B31.3), plus an ISO choice. Check aws.org for the editions currently examined.

There is no automotive weld quality specification on that list. Automotive candidates therefore usually take D1.1: it covers structural steel that most plants have in abundance, and its organization of qualification, fabrication and inspection clauses teaches a way of reading codes that transfers to manufacturers' own standards. Utility and pipeline contractors should consider API 1104. Refinery and power plant maintenance people should look at the ASME option. Bridge inspectors working MDOT jobs can take D1.5. The D1.1 summary and the comparison of API 1104 with D1.1 help you decide.

The six days, adapted for Michigan plants

Day 1 starts with the arc and resistance processes, groove and fillet joint geometry, the standard vocabulary of AWS A3.0 and the symbol system of AWS A2.4. Automotive candidates often know gas metal arc and resistance welding very well and need extra practice on shielded metal arc, submerged arc and gas tungsten arc, which appear in the exam regardless of local practice.

Day 2 is metallurgy, mechanical and destructive testing, how discontinuities form, which NDT methods reveal them, safety, and the inspector's duties and ethics. Detroit groups usually spend extra time on high-strength steels, the effects of heat input on hardness, and hydrogen cracking in repair welds on tool steel.

Day 3 prepares for the practical with gauge use, weld size and profile measurement, and visual evaluation against written criteria. When the six days run at a plant, the group uses its own gauges and weld samples from its own lines; Atlantis does not provide replica kits.

Day 4 works through the chosen code book: where the definitions, qualification rules, fabrication requirements and acceptance tables sit, and how to reach them quickly. Day 5 is timed practice papers for all three parts with a full review of every error. Day 6 returns to weak areas and covers exam-day pacing and the AWS application checklist.

Every practice question is drafted by Atlantis from the AWS topic outline, and none comes from a real AWS paper. The course defines what is taught; it cannot promise an exam result.

Experience questions for automotive and plant workers

AWS sets a required number of years of welding-related work according to education; the full scale is on the national page. Five years applies to a welder whose top qualification is a high school diploma. Finishing a trade or vocational welding course cuts that by a year, and a two-year degree in an engineering, engineering technology or physical science field cuts it to two.

Automotive careers raise a particular issue. A weld technician who spent years tuning robots and spot weld controllers has clearly done welding work. A quality engineer who mostly audited paperwork may have a harder case. AWS decides what counts as welding-related experience, so describe your actual duties accurately and keep records of the welding processes and standards involved. The vision requirement is assessed separately on the AWS visual acuity record, and the timing of that eye test must fit the window AWS sets before your exam date.

What comes after the CWI in Detroit

A Detroit CWI then works on the nine-year AWS cycle, filing renewals partway through it and recertifying when it closes. Detroit inspectors who work with structural or plant steel often add NDT skills next. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, an employer certifies its own NDT staff under its written practice, and Atlantis provides training on that basis, starting with VT Level 1; see NDT training in Detroit for local options. The CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II comparison explains how the credentials relate, and visual testing in Detroit shows the inspection service side. For simulated inspection practice, try the welding workshop in Practical NDT.

Candidates around the Great Lakes can compare CWI preparation in Cleveland, Chicago and Milwaukee.

Request a quote for Detroit-area candidates

A useful request lists how many employees are working toward the CWI, the Part C book each has picked, and whether they will study individually online or together at your plant (give the address). Submit it on the Detroit quote request page, and a reply follows within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an automotive code book for Part C?
faq.a: No. The AWS list covers structural, bridge, aluminum, railroad, aerospace, pipeline, ASME and ISO options, but no automotive weld quality specification. Most Detroit automotive candidates choose AWS D1.1.

faq.q: What is the difference between a CWI and a CRWT?
faq.a: Both are AWS credentials. The Certified Resistance Welding Technician focuses on spot and projection welding equipment and setup. The CWI is a broad welding inspection credential built around codes, metallurgy, discontinuities and visual acceptance.

faq.q: Does robot weld cell work count as welding experience?
faq.a: It can, if your role involved welding work such as programming, setting up or troubleshooting the welding process. AWS decides what is welding-related, so describe your duties precisely and keep records.

faq.q: Where is the CWI exam taken near Detroit?
faq.a: Parts A and C are taken by computer at Prometric centers after AWS sends your eligibility code. Part B runs only at AWS seminar locations on set dates; check aws.org for the closest site.

faq.q: Do you run classes at a Detroit location?
faq.a: No. Candidates on their own prepare online with instructor support for questions, and a plant or contractor can have the six days delivered at its own facility. Atlantis offices are located in Houston and Hyderabad.
AWS runs the examination and awards the certificate. The Atlantis role stops at preparation: it never sees the exam papers and holds no AWS endorsement or approval.

faq.q: Which code book suits refinery or power plant maintenance in Michigan?
faq.a: The ASME option, built on Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, fits refinery and power plant work. Gas utility contractors usually prefer API 1104.

faq.q: Are the practice papers taken from past exams?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes every question itself from the topics AWS publishes for each part.

faq.q: Can a supplier train a whole quality team at once?
faq.a: Yes. An employer can book the six days at its own facility for a group, using its own gauges and weld samples. Every member of that group still files a personal AWS application and has to satisfy the experience and eyesight requirements alone.

faq.q: How do I get a quote?
faq.a: Use the Detroit CWI quote form with your headcount, code books and facility location. Atlantis replies within one business day.
